data.name: Sumir
data.gender_notes: Sumir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who adores or worships the Sun. The name Sumir carries the meaning “Worshipper of the Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sumir usually hope their child will grow to embody worshipper of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who seek the light and wisdom of the Sun God
data.etymology: Sumir belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Worshipper of the Sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sumir total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sumir" is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, emphasizing spiritual devotion towards the Sun. The Sun is considered the life-giving force and a symbol of joy, power, and creativity in Hinduism. By giving the name Sumir, parents bestow upon their child an innate connection to the divine power of the Sun. In daily life, this name acts as a reminder to honor and respect the Sun's energy and influence on our lives.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Sumir" embodies the spiritual practice of Sun worship, symbolizing the awakening of the inner Sun – the individual spiritual self. Adoring and connecting to the Sun is an integral part of spiritual growth and enlightenment in Hinduism. The Sun represents consciousness, knowledge, and self-realization. As Sumir, an individual is encouraged to embody the qualities of the Sun, such as strength, vitality, and knowledge, and to continually remember and cherish their connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sumir means "to constantly remember and contemplate upon the divine." It is a name that encourages one to remain focused on the divine presence within and around them, fostering a deep sense of devotion and spiritual connection.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sumir was a famous Hindu king who ruled during the Gupta Empire around 460 AD. The name Sumir carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sumir remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Radha Sumir in Mumbai, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Sumir, which means "Worshipper of the Sun". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
